newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields made hefty gains on Friday, bolstered by all-time high German bund futures.
"It's the German market that has driven all markets today and we closed fairly unchanged spread-wise," one dealer said.
The ten-year bond yield fell eleven basis points to record low 6.98 percent.
"The undertone ahead of next week is strong, but we are dependent on what happens in Germany," he added.
Six-month T-bill rates dropped seven basis points to 4.19 percent and the crown firmed to 4.3600 against the mark compared to 4.3740 late on Thursday.
"We are clearly in a soft mark period. I think the crown will firm to 4.30 against the mark in the next couple of weeks," said James McKay, economist at PaineWebber.
"But it all depends on what happens to the dollar. In our scenario the dollar will weaken to 1.48 against the mark in three months time. The crown will then follow," he added.
Expectations are building up for a Riksbank cut of its interest rate corridor by 50 basis points on December 5.
After the repo rate cut this week to 4.35 percent there is only ten basis point left to the corridor's floor.
